answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact: like a glacier that only moves under real weight, trust accrues slowly and cannot be faked in bulk. A would-be attacker must post a separate bond for each fake identity, and proven abuse forfeits the bond — an onyx-hard cost that scales linearly with the number of sock puppets, while an honest agent pays nothing net because its stake is returned. The fable of free identities ends: creating ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand bonds.
